exact_statement: Let K>=0 and let f be a least-essential-dimension Boolean violation D_K(f)=H(f)-K I(f)>0 of uniform-cube FEI(K). For every nonempty proper physical block A of a coordinates, let w_t be the retained child Fourier row, q_t=E w_t^2, z_t=w_t^2/q_t on positive rows, c_t=E(z_t-1)^2, C_A=sum_t q_t c_t and Gamma_A=sum_t q_t log2(1+c_t). Then C_A>0: identical squared spectra of all physical children are impossible. More quantitatively set h_t=sign(w_t), sign(0)=1, eta_t=min(1,||w_t/sqrt(q_t)-h_t||_2), eta=sum_t q_t eta_t. With psi_a(s)=h2(s)+s log2(2^a-1) up to s=1-2^-a and psi_a(s)=a thereafter, D_K(f)<=Gamma_A+psi_a(eta)+K a eta. Since eta<=sqrt(C_A), if C_A<=1/4 then D_K(f)<=log2(1+C_A)+h2(sqrt(C_A))+sqrt(C_A) log2(2^a-1)+K a sqrt(C_A). This uses FEI(K) on actual Boolean row phases of smaller dimension, not an assumption that phases are physical descendants. Nonstrict physical-descendant ratio criticality alone does not imply C_A>0, as witnessed by a product of two quadratic two-bit signs. No uniform K or FEI resolution follows.
